paragraphs: May Mobility develops autonomous driving technology and brings it to ride-hail platforms, cities, campuses and businesses. Its operations run from rural Minnesota to Atlanta and the dense streets of Japan.

The cornerstone of the technology is a system the company calls Multi-Policy Decision Making. It is described as a real-time, reinforcement-learning AI algorithm. Vehicles generate training examples relevant to their current environment and learn while driving. The sensor stack and the decision-making platform work together to monitor the road and run simulations of possible situations and hazards.

An autonomous ride-hail preview is live on Lyft. The site notes a first autonomous vehicle fleet deployed with Lyft in Atlanta. It also lists a strategic partnership with Uber to scale autonomous vehicles. An investment from Grab is tied to expansion into Southeast Asia. The chief executive is Edwin Olson.
